text:
Ava: Hey all — quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Dropping a few clarifying Qs we didn't get to. I'll answer where I can. First: when we say 'unified inference' do we mean feature parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, or mostly a consistent developer experience?

Ravi: Great question. We mean developer experience parity (same API/SDK, same routing semantics) + behavioral parity for core features. Hardware and perf differences will remain; we surface them in the model catalog and docs.

Maya: From product POV: prioritize parity for core surfaces (generation, chat, embeddings). Advanced ops features (canary rollouts, per-route tracing) will reach Dedicated/Private on a staggered cadence.

Jordan: How should we frame differentiation against competitors on the external one-pager? e.g., "cost-aware controls" and "graceful degradation" sound right but want concise phrasing.

Sam: For sales: customers really ask about predictable cost and migration path from Hosted -> Dedicated. We should make that path explicit in collateral.

Ava: Agreed. Messaging should call out predictable unit economics, transparent benchmarks/evals, and an easy migration story. Also mention our runtime and cache/batching levers as concrete knobs.

Ravi: To be explicit on thesis vs competitors: we're not trying to be a model training provider or just a model catalog. We're the inference-serving layer: latency/cost/reliability + ops that let teams ship.

Maya: Roadmap clarity request: can we share rough prioritization? My suggestion: 1) runtime perf and kernel selection, 2) observability and rollouts, 3) onboarding and migrations.

Jordan: Any quantitative targets for those? e.g., p99 latency reduction, token-cost improvements?

Ravi: High-level targets: aim for ~10-20% p99 improvement for targeted workloads via kernel optimizations and batching. Cost goal: ~15% unit cost reduction through smarter caching/batching and model quantization suggestions. These are workload-dependent, not guarantees across every model.

Sam: When do we start GTM messaging for Private? Need to know for AE decks and case studies.

Ava: Soft messaging to sales and partners next month. Public case studies and top-line collateral in 6–8 weeks — focus initially on finance and healthcare verticals.

Maya: Quick technical question from eng: how will automatic fallback to cheaper model variants work in Dedicated if capacity is constrained? Will customers be surprised?

Ravi: It's policy-driven. We won't silently downgrade without opt-in. Default routes are conservative (no fallback). There will be opt-in templates like `latency-first` and `cost-first` you can apply per-route. Console and SDK will expose the policy.

Jordan: Implementation note: ensure we document known compatibility caveats (e.g., small-quantized variants may change tokenization/outputs). I'll draft a short tech note.

ops-bot: Meeting notes uploaded: /files/all-hands/1719004321-notes.pdf :page_with_curl:

Ava: Thanks — I'll post a short FAQ excerpt and a couple of slide snippets. If anyone has succinct competitor language or specific metrics they'd like pulled into the one-pager, DM me or drop drafts here.

Sam: :thumbsup: will draft the messaging and a migration checklist, will post by EOD tomorrow.

Maya: I'll add timelines to the public roadmap item and tag eng for dependencies.

Ravi: Happy to review the wording on the kernel/quant notes.

Ava: Great. Closing this thread for now — follow-ups welcome here or in DMs. :sparkles:
